subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron runs get an explicit `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or keep the current per-job `toolsAllow` plus delivery-safeguard model?
rationale: The answer defines a scheduled-run tool-access boundary and public config precedence contract, so automation should not choose the security guarantee or upgrade behavior.

options.title: Add Explicit Cron Policy
options.body: Add `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence against current policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, plus cron delivery regression tests.

options.title: Inherit Subagent Policy
options.body: Make cron sessions reuse `tools.subagents.tools` semantics, accepting a simpler config surface while documenting compatibility impact on existing jobs.

options.title: Keep Current Model
options.body: Decline the new config surface and document per-job `toolsAllow`, creator-derived caps, and delivery safeguards as the supported mitigation.

recommendation.title: Add Explicit Cron Policy
recommendation.body: Add `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence against current policy layers and per-job `toolsAllow`, plus cron delivery regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current source, issue-review, and config/security policy history for this boundary.
